When you went to fight the Ender Dragon, the altar gates opened. You walked into the End and fought the one Gate Dragon still living.
“You, in a dream the universe remembers—like all who ever lived, and loved, and were forgotten—have reached the end.”
Two voices traded words. You could not quite follow. But you knew that this was not the end.

Every time you load a world, fell your first tree, see the first zombie of the first night—you are doing what those Builders did. They did it thousands of years ago. You are doing it now. And maybe thousands of years from now another player will open a Minecraft world and see the ruins of your village, your end ship, your redstone machines.
And they will stop and ask: “Who built this?”
